title: Correlation comparisons and critical curves for disordered XY models
abstract: We prove a lower comparison for disorder-averaged ferromagnetic XY correlations: independent nonnegative random couplings $K_e$ can be replaced by $-\frac12\log\mathbb{E}e^{-2K_e}$. Ginibre's inequality makes each normalized correlation convex in $1-e^{-2K_e}$, so conditional Jensen and thinning compare Bernoulli bond densities; two star-wise Jensen passes handle site dilution on bipartite graphs. Together with the phase-existence theorem of Dario and Garban, these comparisons give local Lipschitz regularity of both the averaged algebraic-phase and susceptibility-divergence thresholds throughout the supercritical density intervals on $\mathbb{Z}^2$. The clean finite-domain criterion of van Engelenburg and Lis also yields explicit finite-size susceptibility lower bounds in a weak-dilution region. For bounded centered bond noise, the possible suppression of the algebraic-phase temperature is at most quadratic in the noise amplitude. Finally, at finite positive thresholds we prove total-variation continuity for bounded iid coupling laws whose essential supremum equals the common support cap, with local Lipschitz control when the reference law has an atom at that cap.
summary: This paper provides rigorous mathematical proofs concerning the stability and regularity of the algebraic phase transition in the disordered 2D XY model. Using advanced comparison inequalities, the authors establish that the critical thresholds remain locally Lipschitz with respect to disorder strength. This work provides deep theoretical insights into how disorder affects critical phenomena in continuous spin systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates the survival and regularity of the algebraic phase transition in the two-dimensional ferromagnetic XY model when subjected to quenched disorder (bond or site dilution).
main_result: The authors establish local Lipschitz regularity for the critical thresholds ($ eta_c^{\star}$) in the supercritical density intervals and prove that the temperature suppression due to bounded noise is at most quadratic in the noise amplitude.
method: The analysis heavily relies on advanced comparison techniques, including Ginibre's inequality, Jensen's inequality, and specialized thinning/dilution comparisons derived from graph theory and probability theory.
model_or_system: The system is the two-dimensional ferromagnetic XY model defined on a lattice ($\mathbb{Z}^2$) with interactions governed by cosine terms, subjected to random bond or site disorder.
key_observables: Averaged XY two-point correlation functions, the critical temperature/threshold ($ eta_c^{\star}$), and the magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$).
important_parameters: Disorder density ($p$), temperature ($ eta$), and the amplitude of the noise ($\epsilon$).
main_assumptions: The analysis builds upon the phase-existence theorem of Dario and Garban, and comparisons are often derived for finite graphs before taking the infinite volume limit.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the 'two-pass mechanism' for site dilution, and Figure 2 illustrates the finite-domain boundary criterion used to obtain bulk bounds.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by establishing rigorous lower bounds for correlations under disorder using various comparison inequalities, deriving the regularity of the critical curve $c(p)$, and finally analyzing the effect of weak noise and total variation convergence on the critical thresholds.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the rigorous mathematical techniques involving correlation inequalities, phase transitions, and stability under perturbations (like noise) are highly relevant to understanding quantum phase transitions in disordered quantum systems.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Stars in one bipartition class have disjoint edge sets even when they share a vertex. Sequential Jensen first averages one class and then the other, multiplying the transformed coupling by r at each pass. The arrows compare averaged correlations, not individual disorder configurations. Here C is a fixed integer-charge cosine correlation.

Figure 2: The finite-domain boundary criterion and the disorder comparison give at least one unit from each shell in its own free square. Ginibre monotonicity preserves these bounds in the outer square. Summing disjoint shells and adding the physical diagonal gives (24); summing over bulk centers gives (25). The shell estimate does not assert a pointwise finite-box lower bound.
